Lisuride, in turn, binds to Htr2a, indicating a possible pathway through which Droperidol may influence Htr2a. The lowest common ancestor of Droperidol and Lisuride is the Agent Affecting Nervous System, suggesting a shared functional role in the nervous system. This integrated pathway implies that Droperidol may exert its effects via Lisuride, which then interacts with Htr2a, potentially modulating its activity. The evidence supports a mechanistic link between Droperidol and Htr2a, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
